attractions.name: Schönbrunn Palace, Vienna
attractions.desc: The former summer residence of the Habsburg emperors, its 1,441 rooms set within extensive formal gardens featuring a hilltop gloriette with sweeping city views. Highlights include the Great Gallery, used for state receptions, and the world's oldest zoo, founded in the palace grounds in 1752. A full visit easily fills half a day.

attractions.name: Hallstatt
attractions.desc: A lakeside village so picturesque it has been reproduced as a full-scale replica in China, with pastel houses stacked against a steep mountainside above the Hallstättersee lake. Beneath the town, one of the world's oldest salt mines is open for tours, complete with a slide used by miners for centuries. Its popularity means visiting early or late in the day helps avoid the crowds.

attractions.name: Vienna State Opera
attractions.desc: One of the most important opera houses in the world, hosting a different production most nights of its packed season. Standing-room tickets are famously cheap and offer a way to experience world-class performances on a budget. Guided daytime tours cover the building's ornate interior even without attending a show.

attractions.name: Hofburg Palace, Vienna
attractions.desc: The former principal imperial palace, now housing the Austrian president's office alongside museums covering the Habsburg treasury, the Spanish Riding School's Lipizzaner horses, and Sisi's personal apartments. Its scale reflects six centuries of continuous expansion by successive rulers. It sits at the heart of Vienna's compact historic center.

attractions.name: Salzburg's Old Town
attractions.desc: Mozart's birthplace and the setting for much of The Sound of Music, its baroque old town sits below the hilltop Hohensalzburg Fortress. Narrow lanes lead past the composer's childhood home and numerous churches, with the fortress offering panoramic Alpine views. It's an easy day trip or overnight stop between Vienna and the mountains.

attractions.name: Wachau Valley
attractions.desc: A UNESCO-listed stretch of the Danube lined with vineyard terraces, medieval castle ruins, and small wine towns like Dürnstein and Melk. A river cruise or bike path along the valley floor is the classic way to see it, with Melk Abbey's baroque library as a highlight. Apricot orchards add a distinct local specialty to the wine.

itinerary.label: Days 1–3
itinerary.title: Vienna
itinerary.desc: Schönbrunn Palace, the Hofburg, and an evening at the State Opera.
itinerary.cost: Schönbrunn Palace entry costs about €26 for the Grand Tour; standing-room opera tickets can be as little as €10–15.
itinerary.food: A proper Wiener schnitzel at a traditional Beisl (Viennese tavern) is worth the modest splurge over a tourist-menu version.

itinerary.label: Day 4
itinerary.title: Wachau Valley
itinerary.desc: A day trip along the Danube's vineyard terraces and Melk Abbey.
itinerary.cost: Melk Abbey entry costs about €14; a Danube river cruise segment runs €20–30.
itinerary.food: Try apricot specialties (jam, schnapps, strudel) — the Wachau Valley is Austria's apricot-growing region.

itinerary.label: Days 5–6
itinerary.title: Salzburg
itinerary.desc: Mozart's old town and the hilltop Hohensalzburg Fortress.
itinerary.cost: Hohensalzburg Fortress entry with the funicular costs about €16.
itinerary.food: A Mozartkugel chocolate from a traditional confectioner is the classic Salzburg souvenir and snack in one.

itinerary.label: Days 7–9
itinerary.title: Hallstatt & the Salzkammergut
itinerary.desc: The lakeside village, its ancient salt mine, and the surrounding alpine lake district.
itinerary.cost: The Hallstatt salt mine tour costs about €36; the skywalk viewpoint adds a few more euros.
itinerary.food: Try fresh lake fish (reinanke or char) at a lakeside restaurant in Hallstatt — a genuine regional specialty.

goodToKnow.tipping: Round up or add roughly 10% in restaurants, handed directly to the server
goodToKnow.safety: Very safe; normal city precautions in central Vienna
goodToKnow.gettingAround: Trains link cities efficiently; a car helps for the Salzkammergut lakes
goodToKnow.gettingThere: Vienna International Airport (VIE) is the natural start for this route; Salzburg Airport (SZG) works if you'd rather begin in the west and travel it in reverse

food.name: Wiener schnitzel
food.desc: A thin, breaded and fried veal cutlet, one of Austria's most iconic dishes.

food.name: Sachertorte
food.desc: A dense chocolate cake with a thin apricot jam layer, invented in Vienna in 1832.

food.name: Apfelstrudel
food.desc: Thin pastry wrapped around spiced apples, usually served warm with cream.

food.name: Melange coffee
food.desc: Vienna's classic coffeehouse drink, similar to a cappuccino, best enjoyed slowly.

faq.q: How long can I stay in Austria without a visa?
faq.a: 90 days within any 180-day period for US, UK, Canadian, and Australian passport holders — the standard Schengen rule. The EU's EES biometric border system is now active, so budget extra time at your first entry.

faq.q: Which airport should I fly into?
faq.a: Vienna International (VIE) for this route; Salzburg Airport (SZG) if you'd rather begin in the west and travel it in reverse.

faq.q: Do I need to book Schönbrunn Palace in advance?
faq.a: Recommended in peak season — timed-entry slots can sell out on busy summer days, though it's less essential than, say, Neuschwanstein in neighboring Germany.
Comparable to Germany — moderate by Western European standards, with Vienna running a bit higher than Salzburg or the lake district.

daysReason: 9 days covers Vienna, the Wachau Valley, Salzburg, and the Salzkammergut lakes without rushing. 6 works if you drop one region; 12+ lets you add Innsbruck and the western Alps.
visa: Not required for EU, UK, US, and Canadian citizens for stays up to 90 days — always confirm current rules before booking.

attractions.name: Palácio de Schönbrunn, Viena
attractions.desc: A antiga residência de verão dos imperadores Habsburgo, com as suas 1.441 divisões situadas dentro de jardins formais extensos com um mirante no topo de uma colina com vistas amplas sobre a cidade. Os destaques incluem a Grande Galeria, usada para receções de estado, e o jardim zoológico mais antigo do mundo, fundado nos terrenos do palácio em 1752. Uma visita completa ocupa facilmente meio dia.

attractions.name: Hallstatt
attractions.desc: Uma vila à beira-lago tão pitoresca que foi reproduzida à escala real na China, com casas em tons pastel empilhadas contra uma encosta íngreme acima do lago Hallstättersee. Debaixo da vila, uma das minas de sal mais antigas do mundo está aberta a visitas, completa com um escorrega usado pelos mineiros durante séculos. A sua popularidade significa que visitar de manhã cedo ou ao fim do dia ajuda a evitar as multidões.

attractions.name: Ópera Estatal de Viena
attractions.desc: Uma das casas de ópera mais importantes do mundo, acolhendo uma produção diferente na maioria das noites da sua temporada carregada. Os bilhetes de pé são famosamente baratos e oferecem uma forma de assistir a espetáculos de classe mundial com orçamento limitado. Visitas guiadas diurnas cobrem o interior ornamentado do edifício mesmo sem assistir a um espetáculo.

attractions.name: Palácio de Hofburg, Viena
attractions.desc: O antigo palácio imperial principal, hoje albergando o gabinete do presidente austríaco ao lado de museus que cobrem o tesouro Habsburgo, os cavalos Lipizzano da Escola de Equitação Espanhola, e os aposentos pessoais de Sisi. A sua escala reflete seis séculos de expansão contínua por sucessivos governantes. Situa-se no coração do centro histórico compacto de Viena.

attractions.name: Cidade Velha de Salzburgo
attractions.desc: Local de nascimento de Mozart e cenário de grande parte de A Noviça Rebelde, a sua cidade velha barroca situa-se abaixo da Fortaleza Hohensalzburg no topo de uma colina. Ruas estreitas passam pela casa de infância do compositor e por numerosas igrejas, com a fortaleza a oferecer vistas alpinas panorâmicas. É uma excursão de um dia fácil ou paragem noturna entre Viena e as montanhas.

attractions.name: Vale de Wachau
attractions.desc: Um trecho classificado pela UNESCO do Danúbio ladeado de socalcos de vinha, ruínas de castelos medievais, e pequenas cidades vinícolas como Dürnstein e Melk. Um cruzeiro fluvial ou ciclovia ao longo do vale é a forma clássica de o ver, com a biblioteca barroca da Abadia de Melk como destaque. Pomares de alperce acrescentam uma especialidade local distinta ao vinho.

itinerary.label: Dias 1–3
itinerary.title: Viena
itinerary.desc: O Palácio de Schönbrunn, o Hofburg, e uma noite na Ópera Estatal.

itinerary.label: Dia 4
itinerary.title: Vale de Wachau
itinerary.desc: Uma excursão de um dia ao longo dos socalcos de vinha do Danúbio e a Abadia de Melk.

itinerary.label: Dias 5–6
itinerary.title: Salzburgo
itinerary.desc: A cidade velha de Mozart e a Fortaleza Hohensalzburg no topo da colina.

itinerary.label: Dias 7–9
itinerary.title: Hallstatt e o Salzkammergut
itinerary.desc: A vila à beira-lago, a sua antiga mina de sal, e a região de lagos alpinos circundante.

goodToKnow.tipping: Arredonda para cima ou acrescenta cerca de 10% em restaurantes, entregue diretamente ao empregado
goodToKnow.safety: Muito seguro; precauções normais de cidade no centro de Viena
goodToKnow.gettingAround: Os comboios ligam bem as cidades; um carro ajuda para os lagos do Salzkammergut
goodToKnow.gettingThere: Vienna International Airport (VIE) is the natural start for this route; Salzburg Airport (SZG) works if you'd rather begin in the west and travel it in reverse

food.name: Wiener schnitzel
food.desc: Um escalope de vitela fino, panado e frito, um dos pratos mais icónicos da Áustria.

food.name: Sachertorte
food.desc: Um denso bolo de chocolate com uma fina camada de compota de alperce, inventado em Viena em 1832.

food.name: Apfelstrudel
food.desc: Massa fina enrolada à volta de maçãs especiadas, normalmente servida quente com natas.

food.name: Café melange
food.desc: A bebida clássica dos cafés vienenses, semelhante a um cappuccino, melhor apreciada devagar.
